items.prompt: Black to move. The white king is far away, and the pawn needs four moves to queen. Find a move that saves the draw.
hints: Count the pawn's steps to b8, then draw the square: b4 to b8 up the file, and the same number of files across.
The square reaches the f-file. Which king moves land on the f-file?
Kf6, Kf7 or Kf8.
items.explain: The pawn needs four moves, so its square runs from the b-file to the f-file. Kf6, Kf7 and Kf8 step into it, and the tablebase gives a draw after each. The other five king moves stay outside, and White wins.

feedback_by_move.g7g6: Staying on the g-file leaves the king outside the pawn's square: the pawn runs and White wins.
feedback_by_move.g7h6: The h-file is even further from the pawn: White wins.
feedback_by_move.g7h7: The king stays outside the square: White wins.

items.prompt: The pawn needs four moves; White's king is far away on h1. White to move. Black's king is on g6. What is the result with best play?
hints: Is Black's king inside the square of the pawn?
White moves first, so the square shrinks before Black can step in.
The pawn runs: White wins.
items.explain: With White to move, the pawn steps to b5 and Black's king can no longer step into the smaller square. The tablebase gives White the win, and b5 is the only winning move.

items.prompt: The same position, but Black is to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Only the side to move has changed.
Can Black's king step onto the f-file now?
Yes: Kf5, Kf6 or Kf7 gets into the square and catches the pawn.
items.explain: With Black to move the king steps into the square (Kf5, Kf6 or Kf7) and the tablebase gives a draw. One tempo turned a win into a draw.

items.prompt: The black king is on g7 instead of g6. White to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Which parts of the picture are the same as the first position?
The king is still on the g-file.
Same result as the first position.
items.explain: Moving the king one rank along the g-file changes nothing: it is still one file outside the square, and the tablebase again gives White the win.

items.prompt: The pawn is on b4 and White's king is far away on h1. Black's king is on f6, Black to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Is the black king inside the square?
The square covers files b to f.
The king is inside and catches the pawn.
items.explain: Black's king is inside the pawn's square and the white king is too far to help, so the tablebase gives a draw.

items.prompt: Black to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Where is White's king compared with the pawn?
A king beside the pawn can protect its path.
White's king escorts the pawn; Black's king cannot stop it.
items.explain: Black's king is inside the pawn's square, but White's king stands next to the pawn on a5 and the tablebase gives White the win. The square rule counts only the pawn and the defending king.

items.prompt: The white king is on h2 instead of h1. Black's king is on f6, Black to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Is the white king any closer to the pawn?
One square along the edge changes nothing here.
Draw.
items.explain: A white king that is still on the far edge cannot help the pawn: the tablebase again gives a draw.

items.prompt: White to move. Each pawn needs three moves to queen, and White moves first. What is the result with best play?
hints: Who queens first? What will the new queen attack?
White's new queen stands on a8. Look along the long diagonal.
It attacks h1, where Black must queen.
items.explain: White queens first, and the new queen on a8 attacks h1, where Black's pawn must queen. The tablebase gives White the win, and a6 is the only winning move.

items.prompt: The white pawn is on the b-file instead. White to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Who queens first now? Where will the new queen stand?
Does a queen on b8 reach Black's queening square?
The race is still equal, but the first queen wins nothing.
items.explain: The pawn still queens first, but the tablebase gives only a draw: queening first is not enough by itself.

items.prompt: Back to the a-pawn, but Black's king is on h7. White to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: What does the black king's rank change about the race?
It is still too far from the a-pawn.
Same as the first position.
items.explain: Moving Black's king one square along the h-file changes neither pawn's path, and the tablebase again gives White the win.

items.prompt: White to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Count the moves each pawn needs.
White's pawn needs four, Black's pawn needs three.
Black queens first and wins.
items.explain: White's pawn is one step short, so Black queens first. The tablebase gives Black the win even though White moves first.

items.prompt: Black to move. What is the result with best play?
hints: Which side's pawn is running, and which way?
The white king is far away from the pawn's path.
The pawn runs and queens.
items.explain: This is the earlier position with the colours reversed and the board turned over: with Black to move, the tablebase gives Black the win.

items.prompt: White to move. Only one move wins. Which?
hints: The pawn pushes both draw. Look at the other piece.
The white king is not as far away as it looks.
Kg2.
items.explain: Only Kg2 wins; the pawn pushes and the other king moves draw. The pawn alone would not be enough here, so White's king has to join in.

feedback_by_move.b2b4: Pushing two squares lets Black's king into the square: draw.
feedback_by_move.b2b3: A single step also lets Black's king into the square: draw.
feedback_by_move.h1g1: A king move along the first rank does not help: draw.
feedback_by_move.h1h2: A king move along the edge does not help: draw.

items.prompt: You are White. Win the race: queen first, then use the queen's reach.

claims.statement: The goal (win) is achievable: the tablebase result for the side to move is a win.

hints: Count both pawns before you move.
Push the a-pawn every move; the king stays home.
When Black queens on h1, your queen on a8 can take it.
items.explain: The tablebase says White wins from here; a6 is the only winning first move.

items.prompt: You are Black. Catch the pawn: hold the draw against best play.

claims.statement: The goal (hold) is achievable: the tablebase result for the side to move is a draw.

hints: Count the pawn's steps and draw its square.
Step into the square on your first move.
Kf6, Kf7 or Kf8, then keep your king in front of the pawn.
items.explain: The tablebase says Black can draw from here; Kf6, Kf7 and Kf8 are the only drawing first moves.
